newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: AWB Report-Australian wheat rises on drought fears.
newsitem.headline: AWB Report-Australian wheat rises on drought fears.

text.p: Australia's domestic wheat market remained weather-driven this week, the Australian Wheat Board (AWB) said in its weekly grain market report.

Prices firmed significantly by A$10.00-A$15.00 a tonne on grower bids because of El Nino drought concerns and domestic new crop yields, the AWB said. "The market will continue to monitor this closely for signs of yield cutbacks particularly in the most moisture sensitive areas of southern New South Wales (NSW), Victoria and South Australia (SA)," the board said.

Reasonable subsoil moisture in Western Australia (WA) and northern NSW is maintaining good crop condition and reasonable development, it said. Queensland fields need more moisture to maintain crop development, the AWB said.
Sydney Futures Exchange wheat futures contracts have gained A$30.00 a tonne since the beginning of the month and this week's AWB tender produced a record volume of 400,000 tonnes bid.
However, the AWB said significant rain in southern Australia would reverse this trend.
The feedgrain market followed a similar trend with old crop sorghum rising by A$15.00 a tonne in Queensland.
This trend was also influenced by the rallying corn and wheat markets in the U.S. and lack of seller interest.
"As a weather-driven trend, the prices will remain fragile," the AWB added.
Ports were active in NSW, SA and WA this week with significant loads going to Indonesia, Japan, Oman and Tanzania, while Queensland and Victoria were relatively quiet, it said.
